name: Atmospheric CO₂
summary: CO₂ 428.6 ppm at Mauna Loa in the week of 1 Nov, up 3.36 ppm on a year, above the 3 ppm Alert line
state: Mauna Loa recorded 428.57 ppm in the week of 1 Nov, 3.36 ppm higher than a year earlier and above the 3 ppm per year Alert line (NOAA GML). That is up from 427.28 ppm the week before. Weekly growth figures are noisy, and no newer weekly reading was available on 13 Nov; El Niño years tend to bring faster CO₂ growth as tropical land absorbs less carbon.
for_you: Faster CO₂ growth means warming continues at pace, with more frequent heat and rainfall extremes over time.

sources.title: NOAA GML — Trends in atmospheric CO₂ at Mauna Loa

why: CO₂ concentration is the main long-run driver of warming; the growth rate shows whether emissions cuts are biting.
drivers: Fossil emissions, land sinks, El Niño (weakens sinks), wildfires.
